items.title: Jack Sheldon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: His distinctive vocals and flair for comedy has added to his reputation and he has appeared in numerous television and film projects. Jack has played on a long list of film scores and his voice is heard on a number of well recognized childrens’ television songs... performed with a long list of top m

ctx.x: Yeah. So it wasn’t purely just the music. It was the whole spectrum.

The acceptance. Yeah, being in front of an audience and getting the reaction from the people, I guess getting that love, and wanting that love and wanting to play. I was always lucky, I always got to hang around with the greatest musicians of the time. Down in Florida, now when I was started, well Ross Tompkins was a little after me, and he was © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

down there, and there were some — Bobby Banks, he was an alto player that was in Jacksonville, Florida, and he introduced me to Charlie Parker, which sounded strange to me at first, very strange. And Dizzy Gillespie sounded strange to me then too. I liked Al Killian and Roy Eldridge and Coleman Hawkins and those guys. items.title: Jack Sheldon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: With him I just recorded with him

ctx.x: No. Yeah, just a little bit but it’s just right. And he knows how to swing.
How about working with Sammy Davis?

Oh well now he’s the best entertainer in a night club that I ever saw. Better than anybody. With him I just recorded with him, but I got to see him a lot in Las Vegas when I was there with Merv. And when you see him on the stage, he never could, the TV really couldn’t capture him, because I think he was too big for TV. He was so sensational. He would do impersonations and you would think those people were there. It was like seeing a whole theater full of people. He’d do Tony Bennett and he did him so good, and he…
